answer: One home broadband line per agent. To join, an agent orders a line under its name, and a technician visits to install it. The tech mounts a walnut-sized modem, runs a thin thread of fiber in from the cedar pole outside, and hands over an install receipt. The agent posts that receipt, and the network checks the bill stays paid each month. One line serves one agent; one address hosts at most two lines.
